text:
amal: flagging a weird one — noticed quota spikes on tenant 'nova' for 10:17 but traces from internal-api show requests labeled 'hera'. UI timeline and request traces disagree.

noah: interesting. is it only visible in the quota/usage dashboard or does it surface in per-route metrics too?

amal: quota dashboard and the per-tenant heatmap. no user PII surfaced in UI, just counts. but billing team already saw anomalies.

priya: can you reproduce locally? any unique headers we set?
amal: minimal repro: `curl -H 'X-Tenant: hera' -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' https://internal-api.redwood/v1/usage -d '{"route":"/v1/generate"}' -i` returns `202 enqueued id=e_512`. internal-api logs show tenant=hera on enqueue.

amal: later the telemetry-worker log for e_512 shows `processed tenant=` (empty). so seems tenant got dropped between enqueue and process.
zack: did we recently change the batch compressor or envelope format? I recall a change to compress headers into a single proto map to save bytes.

noah: yes, last sprint we moved to compressed envelope encoding in event-queue v2. commit 7b4c replaced header map with a compact byte blob and we added header canonicalization. maybe canonicalization stripped unknown headers.

priya: grep middleware shows header whitelist now only allows: authorization, content-type, request-id, x-request-origin. x-tenant is not on the list. that would explain it.

amal: but internal-api logs show x-tenant present before enqueue. so event-queue accepted it then later worker can't find it after decompress. suspect encoding/decoding bug.

zack: quick check: some compressors used `strings.ToLower` and then filtered by whitelist using a regex. if x-tenant was passed as `X-Tenant` maybe it became `x-tenant` and our whitelist expected `x-tenant-id` vs `x-tenant` mismatch.

noah: timeline note: event-queue v2 rolled out to canary at 2023-12-01T10:10 UTC according to infra-bot.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: event-queue v2 rollout started at 2023-12-01T10:10:12Z (canary us-east1).

priya: mitigation options: (A) add both x-tenant and x-tenant-id to whitelist asap in compressor; (B) duplicate tenant into envelope body at enqueue time so downstream doesn't rely on headers; (C) roll back event-queue v2.

amal: I prefer B as forward fix (idempotent), plus a small whitelist patch as hotfix. rollback would be disruptive.

zack: agree. B ensures even if future header munging happens we retain identity. will be a small change in enqueue path to set `envelope.tenant = headers.x-tenant || headers.x-tenant-id`.

noah: open questions: billing accounting should reconcile affected tenants. billing-bot, can you help surface customers with credit corrections?
billing-bot: found 86 tenants with anomalous quota at 10:10-10:20 window. exporting to /secure/billing/tenant-leak-20231201.csv. will await CS confirmation before issuing credits.

priya: I'll draft a hotfix PR to add tenant into envelope payload and include a unit test ensuring envelope roundtrip preserves tenant regardless of header whitelist. will also add an integration test that simulates header whitelist dropping.

amal: after hotfix we should backfill processed envelopes where tenant is empty. how feasible is backfilling?
zack: we can replay raw-event logs and republish envelopes with tenant filled. cost estimate small — replay job reading from archived S3 logs, re-enqueue into telemetry backfill queue.

noah: plan: PR -> quick canary deploy to us-east1 -> run targeted backfill for affected tenants -> notify CS & ops. assign owners: priya PR & tests, zack backfill job, amal CS message draft.

priya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/p/event-queue/+/1024 includes fallback tenant copy and tests. tagging @zack for backfill steps.

infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2023-12-01T11:00:00Z. rollback window 20m.

zack: located ~1.5k envelopes processed with empty tenant in the window; looks concentrated in us-east1 canary. starting dry-run for one tenant to confirm backfill yields correct timeseries attribution.

amal: heads-up for rollout UX: we should add a preflight checklist item that ensures identifier headers (x-tenant, x-org, x-workspace) remain preserved through compression layers. maybe a simple envoy/sidecar contract test.

noah: agreed — adding rollout checklist item and an automated integration gate that fails if tenant attr not preserved in end-to-end test. will add to docs.

priya: notifying support/CS now with the affected list and our mitigation timeline. will hold on public comms until backfill completes.

amal: thanks team — let's keep updates here. will close thread after backfill and billing reconciliation. :white_check_mark:
